'Choose which work order gets the lines, or a new one, before drafting
'Yes
'For a work order that cannot take lines, the menu now still opens and offers only a new work order, instead of creating one without asking or listing the old work order with a reason.

'Before (22 Sep spec): on an inspection whose work order is Complete, Invoiced, Paid or Declined, pressing Build lines created a new work order straight away ('the system will create a new work order without asking'); another line of the same spec said a destination that cannot take lines 'will keep its place in the menu and say why'. Now (14 Oct spec): 'the destination menu still opens and offers only a new work order', and the keep-its-place rule is deleted ('a target that cannot be used is not shown'). Same action, different screen and outcome: the tester now sees a menu offering only 'A new work order', and nothing is created until they choose it.

'S2-R5: 29 Sep 2026 (QA contradiction pass answered)
S2-R15: 29 Sep 2026 (QA contradiction pass answered)

'When the run-on work order is not eligible (Complete, Invoiced, Paid, Declined, or an invoice already exists), a new work order is created without asking.
A destination that cannot take lines keeps its place in the menu and says why, rather than silently disappearing.

'On the inspection whose work order is not eligible (Complete, Invoiced, Paid or Declined, or it already has an invoice), pressing Build lines still opens the destination menu; no new work order is created without asking.
The menu offers only a new work order. The inspection's own work order is not listed at all: it is not shown greyed out and no reason is given.
Choosing the new work order creates it for the same customer and asset and the drafting starts there (unchanged).

'3. On the ineligible-work-order inspection, confirm a new work order is created without asking, for the same customer and asset.
4. Confirm an ineligible destination keeps its place in the menu and states why.

'1. Open the completed inspection whose work order is not eligible (for example Complete, or already invoiced).
2. Press Build lines.
3. Read the destination menu that opens.
4. Check the inspection's own work order is not in the menu and only a new work order is offered.
5. Choose the new work order.
6. Check a new work order is created for the same customer and asset and the drafting starts on it.

'Decided by the product manager on 29 Sep. The 22 Sep spec contradicted itself (one line said no menu, another implied the old work order stayed in the menu with a reason); the new rule differs from both readings, so this is a change either way. The last expected line is unchanged and kept only to finish the flow.

'After building you land on Lines, the finding is marked done, rebuild asks
'No

'Lines can now be built from an inspection only once: a second Add Lines adds nothing and says where the lines went, no confirmation is asked, and the completed inspection and the work order note show the outcome instead of Build lines.

'Before (22 Sep spec): 'If lines have already been added from this inspection, the user will be asked to confirm before adding a second set.' The tester was asked to confirm, and a second set was then added. Now (14 Oct spec): 'An inspection is built from once ... no entry point offers the build action again: the completed inspection, the work order note and the asset row show the outcome instead ... if the inspection was built from elsewhere in the meantime, nothing is added and the user is told where the lines went.' There is no confirmation; a second Add Lines adds nothing and says where the lines went, and Build lines is no longer offered.

'S2-R13: 29 Sep 2026 (QA contradiction pass answered)
S3-R8: 29 Sep 2026 (QA contradiction pass answered)
S4-R5: 29 Sep 2026 (QA contradiction pass answered)
S5-R9: 29 Sep 2026 (QA contradiction pass answered)
'If lines were already added from this inspection, the user is asked to confirm before adding a second set, checked when Add Lines is pressed.

'After an inspection's lines have been added, the completed inspection and the work order's inspection report note no longer offer Build lines; each shows the outcome instead ('WO created …' or 'Lines added …') with a link to the work order that got the lines.
If a second set of proposed lines was already open for the same inspection, pressing Add Lines there adds nothing and tells you where the lines went.
No question asking you to confirm a second set appears at any point.
'4. Press Add Lines a second time from the same inspection; confirm you are asked to confirm before a second set is added.

'1. Open the same completed inspection (one not yet built from) in two browser tabs.
2. In the first tab, press Build lines, choose This work order and wait for the proposed lines.
3. In the second tab, press Build lines, choose This work order and wait for the proposed lines.
4. In the first tab, press Add Lines.
5. In the second tab, press Add Lines.
6. Check nothing is added from the second tab, a message says where the lines went, and no question asks you to confirm adding a second set.
7. Open the completed inspection and the work order's inspection report note.
8. Check neither offers Build lines and each shows the outcome with a link to the work order that got the lines.

'Decided on 29 Sep ('an inspection is built from once'); the decision on two users building at the same time was reworded on 7 Oct. The asset's Inspections tab row already showed the outcome after a build on 22 Sep, so it is not part of this change and is left out.

'Building lines with long notes, many findings, or a deleted work order
'Yes
'A second Add Lines no longer adds a duplicate set, and after the run-on work order is deleted the inspection no longer goes back to needing a work order.

'Two users: before (22 Sep spec), 'Duplication happens only if both press Add Lines, which is accepted and recoverable', so the second press added a duplicate set. Now (14 Oct spec): 'When both press Add Lines, only the first adds lines; the second adds nothing and the user is told where the lines went.' Deleted run-on work order: before, where the lines had been added to that work order, 'the inspection counts as needing a work order again', so it was counted in the summary and could be built from again. Now: 'an inspection that has a report survives it as a read-only record ... The inspection does not count as needing a work order, because it can no longer be built from.' It is not counted and offers no Build lines.

'S2-E6: 7 Oct 2026 (Leftovers from the built-once rule; file limit; submit name)
S2-E12: 6 Oct 2026 (Deleted work orders, removed inspections and splits)
S5-E3: 6 Oct 2026 (Deleted work orders, removed inspections and splits)

'If two users draft from the same inspection at once, the drafting itself duplicates nothing; duplication happens only if both press Add Lines, which is accepted and recoverable.
If the run-on work order is deleted, the inspection survives it and stays listed on the asset with a dash in its work order column; any lines added to that work order are gone with it and the inspection counts as needing a work order again.

'If two users draft from the same inspection at once, the drafting duplicates nothing. When both press Add Lines, only the first adds lines; the second adds nothing and is told where the lines went.
If the work order the inspection was run on is deleted, a completed inspection (one that has a report) stays listed on the asset's Inspections tab as a read-only record with a dash in the Work order column.
The inspection does not count as needing a work order again: it offers no Build lines and is not counted in the summary line, because it can no longer be built from.
'4. Repeat, using the second browser to reopen the inspection, and to delete the built lines versus delete the work order; check each result against the expected result below.

'1. Build from a completed inspection with findings, choose This work order (the work order it was run on), and press Add Lines.
2. Open the asset's Inspections tab and note N in the summary line 'N of M have findings with no lines yet'.
3. In the second browser, delete that work order.
4. Reload the asset's Inspections tab and find the inspection.
5. Check it is still listed, with a dash in the Work order column and no Build lines.
6. Check N in the summary line has not gone up.
7. In both browsers, open the completed screen of another completed inspection with findings that has not been built from, press Build lines, choose This work order and wait for the proposed lines.
8. Press Add Lines in the first browser.
9. Press Add Lines in the second browser.
10. Check only one set of lines is added to the work order and the second browser shows a message saying where the lines went.

'Product manager decisions of 6 and 7 Oct; the developer confirmed on 8 Oct that such an inspection is not counted in 'N of M have findings with no lines yet'. Lines added to the deleted work order going with it is unchanged, so it is left out. What happens to an inspection with no report when its work order is deleted is covered by another case, not here.

'The summary card, counts per verdict, and the section review
'Yes
'The findings list now shows one entry per flagged row with all its flagged positions, instead of one entry per flagged position.

'Before (22 Sep spec): the findings list named 'each flagged position as field, axle, row and position with the reading that earned it', so two flagged tires on one row gave two entries. Now (14 Oct spec): it names 'each flagged row as field, axle and row, followed by every flagged position on it with its reading', for example 'Brake & tire measurements · Axle 1 · Tire pressure: left outer 42 psi, right outer 40 psi'. The same two tires now give one entry listing both; a list with one entry per tire now fails.
'S3-R4: 29 Sep 2026 (QA contradiction pass answered)
'The screen leads with a summary card: the completion line, a count per verdict, and a findings list naming each flagged position (field, axle, row, position) with the reading that earned it.

'The findings list has one entry per flagged measurement row, not one entry per flagged tire or brake.
Each entry names the field, the axle and the row, followed by every flagged position on that row with its reading, for example 'Brake & tire measurements · Axle 1 · Tire pressure: left outer 42 psi, right outer 40 psi'.
'1. Read the summary card: completion line, a count per verdict, and the findings list naming each flagged position as field, axle, row and position with its reading.

'1. Add a Per axle field to the template next to the checkbox fields.
2. While filling, on Axle 1 Tire pressure, flag two positions (for example left outer 42 psi and right outer 40 psi, Not OK).
3. Complete the inspection and open its completed screen.
4. Read the findings list on the summary card.
5. Check the two flagged tires appear in one entry for Axle 1 · Tire pressure, listing both positions with their readings.

'Decided on 29 Sep ('one finding per flagged row'). The 22 Sep spec was inconsistent: elsewhere it already said a flagged row produces its own finding. The old check would also pass a list with one entry per tire, which the new one fails. A flagged checkbox field being its own entry is unchanged and is left out.
